## Squachy stopped narcolepsy-ing and I read some legal documents for you

Turns out Squachy's nap had no exit condition. None. Once he fell asleep, he just... stayed asleep, re-triggering the nap every 8 seconds forever, like a cryptid stuck in a `while(true)` loop with no `break`. Multiple people probably thought their board froze. It did not freeze. It was just tired. Fixed: naps now cap at 60 seconds, and he gets a full 10 minutes of quips, bounces, and dramatic patrol walks before he's even allowed to get sleepy in the first place. Napping is the last resort now, not the default state, same as it should be for literally anyone.

Speaking of patrol walks — he used to wander about 40 pixels and call it a day. Weak. He now sprints a full sine cycle from one actual screen edge to the other and back, like he's got somewhere to be. He does not have anywhere to be. He lives in your walls. But now he commits to the bit.

Also snuck in: a FAQ, because apparently "how does this work" needed an actual answer instead of me improvising in Discord DMs forever. And the license changed from MIT to the Common Public License 1.0 — yes, I read the whole thing, yes, it's copyleft now, no, I will not be summarizing contract law for you in this changelog, that's what the FAQ and LICENSE file are for.

### The actually-useful part
- **Fixed:** Squachy's nap could run indefinitely with no way out short of interacting with the device — now capped at 60 seconds, with a cooldown so he doesn't just fall right back asleep
- Idle threshold before he's even eligible to nap raised from 3 minutes to 10, so the fun stuff gets room to happen first
- Patrol walks now run a full edge-to-edge sweep instead of a small fixed wander
- Added `FAQ.md` — what this thing does, hardware options, the web flasher, detection basics, legality, Squachy/Boring Mode, SD logging, touch calibration
- License switched from MIT to CPL-1.0 (copyleft) — see [LICENSE](https://github.com/skizzophrenic/SquachWatch-CYD/blob/master/LICENSE)
- Web flasher now gets its own front-and-center section in the README instead of a footnote
